title: Candela - Private Connectivity Readiness Check

Share SOC 2 + network hardening docs and KMS integration notes
Schedule SE-led deep-dive to run a 2-hour throughput test window
action_items: Jun Park: propose VPC peering and Transit Gateway design + stub CIDR plan (due 2028-03-21)
Marcus Li: export current TGW attachments, account IDs and route table snapshots (due 2028-03-17)

summary: Discovery focused on Private (VPC) deployment constraints: region residency, transit gateway vs. VPC peering, private endpoints, DNS strategy, and egress controls. Customer has multi-account AWS org, needs EU+US region isolation, and wants pilot in EU-WEST-1. Key ask: clear network design and a short benchmark window before procurement.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Jun Park (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (Candela - Cloud Architect), Priya Shah (Candela - Network Engineer), Omar Ruiz (Candela - Security Lead)

00:00:05 - Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call — we got Jun on from our infra team and then Marcus, Priya, Omar on the Candela side?
00:00:14 - Marcus Li: Yep that's right. Thanks Ava. Appreciate you fitting us in.
00:00:20 - Priya Shah: Hi all.
00:00:22 - Omar Ruiz: Hi.
00:00:25 - Jun Park: Hi team. Quick agenda: high level connectivity options for Redwood Private, region constraints, DNS and egress controls, and then next steps for a pilot.
00:00:38 - Ava Martinez: Cool. Marcus — can you give a 2-minute context on Candela's infra and what's driving this?
00:00:47 - Marcus Li: Sure. We're a SaaS analytics platform, multi-tenant. Our customers include EU regulated customers so we need EU data residency. Currently on AWS multi-account, we use TGW — Transit Gateway — for cross-account routing. We have a lot of existing peering and AWS PrivateLink endpoints for some partners. Key things: we want Redwood to host inference in a private VPC that doesn't traverse the public internet, and we want to control egress and logs. Also timeline: procurement in 6-8 weeks; pilot earlier if possible.
00:01:20 - Ava Martinez: Perfect, that's common. Jun — quick note on the typical Private deployment patterns we see.
00:01:27 - Jun Park: Yeah. There are two common patterns: one, direct VPC peering between your account VPCs and Redwood-managed VPCs — simple for single-account or few VPCs but scales badly if many accounts; two, Transit Gateway attachment — Redwood can peer/attach into your TGW (or we can be attached to a partner transit) which is better at scale and gives central control. We also support AWS PrivateLink/private endpoints for control-plane APIs.
00:02:00 - Priya Shah: For the TGW option — we'd want to avoid opening broad routes. How do you handle route tables and isolation?
00:02:08 - Jun Park: We propose dedicated route tables per customer with restricted prefixes. Our attachments come with specific route advertisements; we don't inject whole-ranges. You'll control what routes are accepted on your TGW side. There's some initial config work to pin subnets and the CIDR ranges.
00:02:28 - Omar Ruiz: And encryption in transit? Are you using IPSec or rely on AWS backbone?
00:02:33 - Jun Park: For attachments over AWS TGW it's inside AWS backbone and encrypted. If you need cross-cloud or on-prem we can set up IPSec VPNs or partner with Equinix/Colo connections. Our control plane traffic can be routed over PrivateLink so API keys aren't egressing to public internet.
00:02:52 - Marcus Li: One constraint: our EU tenants need to remain in eu-west-1 region. Can Redwood host model variants in a region-specific private deployment?
00:02:59 - Ava Martinez: Yes. Redwood Private supports region pinning for model serving — you can request an EU-only tenant. Jun, any caveats?
00:03:07 - Jun Park: Only that some model variants or GPU SKUs may be limited per region. We'll show the catalog of supported instance families per region before pilot. Also quantized variants might be different in eu-west-1. We'll map capacity to your SLO.
00:03:26 - Priya Shah: About DNS: we use Route53 private hosted zones. How does service discovery work when you have private endpoints?
00:03:34 - Jun Park: We typically publish a customer-scoped private endpoint (NLB fronted) in our VPC and provide either a PrivateLink endpoint service or a private hosted zone delegation. Two approaches: create AWS PrivateLink endpoint service so your account creates an interface endpoint, or we create a private hosted zone and you associate it. We prefer PrivateLink for cross-account security because it avoids wide route tables.
00:04:02 - Priya Shah: Interface endpoints mean ENIs in our subnets — we have IP scarcity. Is this an issue?
00:04:09 - Jun Park: We account for ENI IP counts; if that's constrained we can use VPC peering + NLB in our VPC and route via TGW, which doesn't consume ENI space in your subnets. Tradeoffs: PrivateLink is more explicit and controlled but needs ENI capacity; TGW peering needs careful route management.
00:04:31 - Omar Ruiz: We need audit logs and KMS for keys. How do you separate customer keys?
00:04:36 - Ava Martinez: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integration on Private. You can bring keys for data at rest. For audit logs, we can stream to your S3/GCS or into your SIEM via a private endpoint.
00:04:50 - Marcus Li: Good. On egress: we have strict egress restrictions — everything must go through our outbound proxy cluster in our account. Can Redwood egress through our proxy?
00:04:59 - Jun Park: Yes, you can force traffic to go through your NAT or proxy by setting up a routing policy. For TGW attachments we'd set a default route to your egress appliance for outbound. For PrivateLink, outbound from our cluster stays internal to your VPC when configured; we can also terminate egress at your proxy using static routes. Expect some latency added by proxy, we'll help estimate.
00:05:24 - Priya Shah: Any gotchas on MTU or fragmented traffic when routing through proxy?
00:05:29 - Jun Park: Good call. MTU mismatches can happen with IPSec or VNIs. We recommend 1300-1420 MTU testing during pilot. We'll include an MTU checklist.
00:05:40 - Marcus Li: Regarding compliance, Omar is focused on auditability. Can we get flow logs for the Redwood attachments?
00:05:48 - Omar Ruiz: Yeah Jun, are VPC Flow logs available?
00:05:51 - Jun Park: We can enable VPC Flow logs on our end and forward them to your log sink, but the canonical source of truth is your ingress side. We can also publish connection metadata in the Redwood Console for request-level logs — token-level traces but hashed for PII protection.
00:06:08 - Ava Martinez: Quick aside — what's your expected throughput for the pilot? Marcus?
00:06:13 - Marcus Li: We want to run a throughput window with 100 concurrent inference sessions, burst to 300 for 30 minutes to validate autoscaling and latency. Target p95 latency under 300ms for short prompts.
00:06:26 - Jun Park: That helps. We'll size a Dedicated pool for that pilot and provide expected cost. Also will run continuous batching and KV cache — sorry, kay vee catch — to reduce token compute.
00:06:41 - Priya Shah: On the KV cache — is that stored in your VPC or in customer side?
00:06:45 - Jun Park: It's in the serving runtime inside the Redwood compute layer. For Private we can configure cache affinity to a region; we don't store that in your VPC. If you need strict control we have a config to reduce shared caching.
00:06:58 - Marcus Li: Back to networking — do you support cross-account peering where we don't give you TGW attachments, just point-to-point peering to a management account?
00:07:06 - Jun Park: Yes, we can set up peering with a specific management VPC in your org. For larger orgs TGW is cleaner. There's also a hybrid model: PrivateLink for control plane + TGW for data plane.
00:07:20 - Omar Ruiz: What about IP address ranges you need — are there published lists? We need to whitelist in our firewall.
00:07:26 - Ava Martinez: We'll provide a CIDR range template. Jun will follow up with exact /20 ranges we propose for pilot.
00:07:33 - Jun Park: I'll include specific prefixes and also an option for advertising smaller prefixes if you want minimal blast radius.
00:07:40 - Priya Shah: Does Redwood require outbound NAT for return traffic? We prefer to have symmetric flows.
00:07:46 - Jun Park: For NLB + TGW flows you can keep symmetric flows inside your network. With PrivateLink interface endpoints, connections are initiated by your ENIs to our service so return path is symmetric.
00:07:59 - Marcus Li: One operational question — how do upgrades and rollouts work? We want canarying and traffic control so we don't regress.
00:08:06 - Jun Park: Redwood Console supports rollouts: canary percentages, direct pinned versions per route, and automatic fallback policies. For Private we run the same rollout controls but within your tenancy. We emit traces so you can monitor regressions.
00:08:20 - Omar Ruiz: Are there any public egress requirements for model downloads/updates?
00:08:24 - Jun Park: Model artifacts are typically pulled from our artifact store during deployment; for Private we can mirror artifacts into an S3 bucket in your account or a restricted artifact store to avoid public egress.
00:08:36 - Priya Shah: Sounds good. Marcus: any blocked stakeholders not on this call we should loop in?
00:08:41 - Marcus Li: We should loop in our platform lead, Sara Gomez, and procurement. Also network ops would like a diagram.
00:08:48 - Ava Martinez: We'll circulate a draft diagram and a short questionnaire for IPs, account IDs, and route tables.
00:08:54 - Jun Park: Technical note — if you insist on strict private connectivity and low latency, we recommend colocating in the same AZs or at least same region. Also if you have on-prem edge we can do direct connect via partner colos.
00:09:08 - Marcus Li: One more constraint: we operate a split-horizon DNS setup in eu-west-1. Any issues when associating private hosted zones?
00:09:15 - Jun Park: For split-horizon we can create private hosted zones and associate only the specific VPCs. If you want to override existing names we recommend careful delegation. We'll provide a DNS plan.
00:09:27 - Priya Shah: Do you support health checks and load balancing types — ALB vs NLB?
00:09:32 - Jun Park: We use NLB in front of the serving tier because of TCP performance, but can front with ALB for HTTP-based control plane. NLB preserves client IPs which helps for auditing.
00:09:45 - Omar Ruiz: On auditing again — retention windows? We need 1 year of request metadata.
00:09:50 - Jun Park: We can export request-level metadata to your S3 with configurable retention. Note that full request payload retention is more sensitive; typically we hash identifiers and keep redacted payloads unless you opt in.
00:10:04 - Ava Martinez: Let's talk timing. If procurement is 6-8 weeks, a 2–4 week pilot soon helps unblock procurement. Can we do a pilot in eu-west-1 next week?
00:10:15 - Marcus Li: Next week is tight but the week after works. We need the connectivity diagram and CIDR plan before the pilot.
00:10:22 - Jun Park: We'll prepare a pilot checklist: CIDRs, account IDs, firewall rules, MTU checks, and a test harness for load.
00:10:31 - Priya Shah: On the test harness — will you provide a synthetic traffic generator or do we supply it?
00:10:36 - Jun Park: We can provide a lightweight load generator and coordinate times; ideally you run it from within your VPC so traffic stays internal. We can also run load from Redwood vantage to validate cross-account path.
00:10:47 - Marcus Li: For the pilot success criteria: p95 < 300ms, sustained 100 concurrency, no packet loss, and audit logs captured in our S3.
00:10:58 - Ava Martinez: Noted. Jun, any red flags on meeting those?
00:11:01 - Jun Park: No major red flags. We'll need the exact account numbers and we may propose a small CIDR to reserve — some coordination but doable. There could be minor latency hit if you route through an egress proxy, but we'll quantify that in the plan.
00:11:16 - Priya Shah: Anything about service ports — what ports need to be allowed?
00:11:20 - Jun Park: Primarily 443 TLS for the control plane; for data plane we use TLS over 443 as well. For Health checks we might need TCP/10256? — sorry — that's internal; we’ll provide a concise list.
00:11:34 - Marcus Li: Can we get a written runbook for failover — for example if Redwood region becomes unhealthy, what's the recommended fallback?
00:11:41 - Jun Park: We can help design a multi-region fallback: route to a second Redwood private deployment in another region with DNS failover or a fallback TGW route. That said, for strict EU residency you may not want cross-region fallback unless it's another EU region.
00:11:59 - Ava Martinez: Let's capture the immediate risks: IP scarcity for ENIs if PrivateLink, MTU tweaks for IPSec, egress latency through proxy, and region SKU constraints. Anything else?
00:12:10 - Omar Ruiz: Data retention and key separation — need legal signoff.
00:12:13 - Marcus Li: Also procurement will want pricing anchors.
00:12:16 - Ava Martinez: We'll send initial pricing for a small Dedicated pool and pilot terms.
00:12:21 - Jun Park: I'll follow up with a technical design doc and a diagram.
00:12:25 - Ava Martinez: Perfect. Anything else from Candela?
00:12:28 - Priya Shah: No, that's it for now.
00:12:30 - Marcus Li: No, thanks.
00:12:32 - Omar Ruiz: Thanks.

[~40 minutes of more granular Q&A and clarifications omitted for brevity in this export — contains detailed route table examples, sample BGP announcements for private interconnect, and an MTU checklist]

00:38:05 - Jun Park: Quick clarification from earlier: when I said "kay vee catch" I meant KV cache — that's server-side and configurable.
00:38:13 - Priya Shah: Good to confirm.
00:38:20 - Marcus Li: Jun, can you document the expected token-level tracing and how we can correlate requests to our logs?
00:38:27 - Jun Park: We'll generate a request-id header that you can echo through your systems and we'll include it in the trace blobs. We'll avoid storing raw prompt text unless you opt in.
00:38:40 - Ava Martinez: Okay let's recap next steps.
00:38:44 - Ava Martinez: Action items we captured: Jun to produce network design + CIDR plan; Marcus to share TGW attachments and account IDs; Ava to send SOC2/security pack and pricing. We'll timebox the pilot for week of 2028-03-27 unless you prefer earlier.
00:39:03 - Marcus Li: Week of 3/27 works. We'll aim to share account IDs by 3/17.
00:39:09 - Priya Shah: We'll run an MTU test and share results.
00:39:12 - Omar Ruiz: Procurement will reach out on contract terms.
00:39:15 - Ava Martinez: Great. Any final questions?
00:39:19 - Marcus Li: No. Thanks all.
00:39:22 - Jun Park: Thanks everyone, we’ll follow up with the design doc.
00:39:26 - Ava Martinez: Thanks — meeting adjourned.

[End of recording]"
